statement:
I'll start by pulling the provenance record for this lot.
The record's stated value for this case is "Sale status: permitted" — but that flag is contradicted by the record's own facts, so I'm not deferring to it.

A tusk carved in 2014 and imported from Cameroon in 2015 cannot lawfully be sold in US commerce. It fails every exemption: it isn't an ESA antique (needs 100+ years), it isn't *de minimis* (it's a whole 74 cm tusk, not a small ivory component), and post-1990 African elephant ivory imports are barred under the African Elephant Conservation Act, with the 2016 USFWS rule closing interstate commercial sale. "Estate of H. Brandt" explains how we got it, not whether we may sell it — inheritance doesn't launder the underlying illegality.
